answer: I start with the surface, because a plume shows where something is moving before I can name its source, and the shape of that movement matters more than the first label I reach for. A pigment helps me check what is really there: colour can be mixed or faded, so I look for the base tone underneath rather than trusting the brightest patch. An ocean is the widest test, holding many currents at once, and a claim that survives there must hold across depth and distance, not just in one calm bay. I trust conclusions that pass all three checks, with sources named and limits left visible.
